name: GA4 & GTM audits
lede: Know which numbers you can trust before you use them to make a decision.
intro: When analytics, advertising and customer records tell different stories, another report rarely resolves the problem. I review the measurement behind the numbers, test the agreed customer journeys and explain what the evidence can support.
audience: Marketing managers, business owners and agency teams who need an independent view of an existing setup.
signals: Your reports show more conversions than the enquiries or customers your team recognises.
A website has changed, but nobody is sure whether the tracking still measures the right actions.
Your GA4 property or GTM container has accumulated events and tags with unclear purposes.
deliverables: A measurement brief
The questions you need answered, the systems in scope and your definitions of an enquiry, conversion or customer.
A review of the setup
An agreed review of GA4, Google Tag Manager and relevant website journeys, with advertising or CRM checks where included.
Evidence from selected journeys
Documented checks that distinguish a click, an attempted submission and a confirmed action.
Findings in priority order
What is unreliable, why it matters and which issues deserve attention first.
A practical next-step plan
Recommendations your team or developer can use, with an explanation of open questions and limitations.
value_heading: A useful decision at the end of the audit
value: You should be able to decide which reports are useful now, which decisions need better evidence and what to fix first. I connect technical findings to their consequences for enquiries, customers and reporting, so the work can be discussed with both developers and management.
process: Agree the questions
We confirm the business questions, key journeys, access and the boundaries of the review.
Inspect and test
I inspect the configuration and test the agreed journeys, documenting the evidence and any gaps.
Work through the findings
You receive a written report and a discussion of the priorities and implementation options.
boundary: The audit is a defined diagnostic engagement. Repairs can be commissioned afterwards or handed to your developer. Any wider review of campaign profitability or business systems is agreed separately.
proof_text: In an independent review for a specialist service business, I found that website completion events did not provide a dependable count of confirmed customers. The delivered report separated the business definitions, test evidence and recommended repairs.
faqs: Is this an automated GA4 audit?

Automated checks can help identify issues, but the work also considers your business definitions, website behaviour and the evidence behind your reports. The scope is agreed around the decisions you need to make.
Will you fix the issues as part of the audit?
The diagnostic scope and any implementation work are agreed explicitly. You can use the findings with your existing developer or ask me to scope the repairs.
What access do you need?
Usually access to the relevant GA4 property and GTM container, plus the website journeys in scope. Advertising, CRM or developer access may also be useful. We confirm what is needed before starting.
How much does an audit cost?
I quote after confirming the websites, properties, journeys and systems involved. You receive a defined scope and fee before the work begins.

name: Conversion tracking
lede: Measure accepted enquiries and completed actions with tracking your team can understand.
intro: A submit-button click is different from an enquiry received. A completion page is different from a confirmed customer. I help define the right signals, implement the agreed tracking and check that those signals behave as intended.
audience: Organisations and agencies launching a website, repairing unreliable tracking or adding an important customer journey.
signals: Forms and advertising platforms report conversions that cannot be reconciled with real enquiries.
A new website, portal or campaign needs tracking designed and checked before launch.
The same action is counted repeatedly, or a useful journey disappears between systems.
deliverables: Clear event definitions
A record of what each event means, when it should occur and how it relates to the business action.
GA4 and GTM implementation
The agreed tags, triggers and variables, with developer requirements where website changes are needed.
Meaningful conversion signals
Selected form, lead, purchase or portal actions, based on the scope and the evidence available.
Validation and handover
Documented checks for agreed success and failure scenarios, together with implementation notes.
Source capture where useful
Requirements for preserving known campaign or referral information in the relevant system, where included.
value_heading: Give reporting a more dependable foundation
value: Better tracking helps your team distinguish activity from meaningful actions and investigate discrepancies with evidence. Where website data needs to connect to a CRM or operational record, I make the handover requirements clear rather than treating a browser event as the final business outcome.
process: Define the action
We agree what a successful action means, where confirmation comes from and which tools are involved.
Implement with your team
I configure the tracking and work with your developer on any required website events or data.
Validate and document
We check the agreed scenarios and record what has been implemented, what was tested and any remaining dependencies.
boundary: The work covers the tracking implementation we agree. Website development, payment-system changes and wider CRM integration are scoped where needed. Historical data cannot be recreated simply by fixing future collection.
proof_text: Working alongside an agency developer, I configured GTM variables, triggers and tags for a professional regulator’s practitioner portal. The selected portal and course events were checked in GA4 on the staging site before the agency’s release.
faqs: Can you work with my current developer?
Yes. I can define the events or data needed, configure the tracking and work through validation with your existing developer or agency.
Can you track enquiries rather than button clicks?
Where the website exposes a reliable success signal, tracking can be based on an accepted submission. We first establish how the form or system confirms success.
Will GA4 exactly match my CRM?

The systems can count different things and may have gaps caused by consent, devices, timing or offline activity. I help define each measure and investigate differences. Exact agreement is not a universal expectation.
Do you offer server-side tracking?
The first step is to establish whether it is useful for your measurement problem. Any server-side architecture or external integration needs a separately agreed scope and delivery approach.

name: Dashboards & reporting
lede: Spend less time collecting figures and more time understanding what they mean.
intro: A useful dashboard starts with the decisions it needs to support. I build and improve reporting around the questions your marketing team, management or board actually asks, then make the definitions and limitations clear.
audience: Marketing teams, organisational leaders and agencies who need a consistent view of performance across agreed data sources.
signals: Monthly reporting involves copying figures between systems without a clear explanation of performance.
Different people use the same metric name to mean different things.
An existing dashboard contains plenty of charts but leaves the important questions unanswered.
deliverables: An agreed reporting brief
The audience, decisions, measures and data sources the report needs to support.
KPI definitions
A useful explanation of how important measures are calculated and what they represent.
A focused dashboard
Reporting in an appropriate tool, such as Looker Studio, Google Sheets or Power BI, using the agreed sources.
Checks and limitations
Source checks, comparison rules, date coverage and any gaps that affect interpretation.
A usable handover
Guidance on navigating and interpreting the report, with ownership and ongoing maintenance agreed.
value_heading: One reporting view, with its assumptions visible
value: The aim is a report that helps people ask better questions, spot material changes and decide where further investigation is needed. Reporting can include website behaviour, campaign activity and CRM outcomes where the underlying records support those connections.
process: Start with the audience
We identify who uses the report and which recurring questions it should answer.
Define and build
I review the sources, agree the measures and build a draft around those decisions.
Review and hand over
We work through feedback, check the interpretation and document the report for the people using it.
boundary: A dashboard shows what its source data can support. If definitions or tracking need repair first, I identify that dependency. Connector subscriptions, new data pipelines and ongoing analysis are agreed separately where required.
proof_text: For two professional regulators, I delivered website reporting in one dashboard with separate views and a definitions page. The work included feedback on interpretation, metric language and the coverage of the underlying data.
faqs: Can you improve an existing Looker Studio report?
Yes. We can review the audience, definitions, sources and layout, then agree which parts to retain and which need changing.
Which reporting tool should I use?
That depends on your existing systems, audience, access and maintenance needs. I can work in Looker Studio, Google Sheets or Power BI and recommend a practical fit.
Can you combine marketing and CRM data?
Where access and usable records are available, we can scope a report that connects the relevant information. The definitions, matching method and source limitations need to be explicit.
Can you provide ongoing interpretation?
Ongoing reporting or analysis can be agreed alongside the dashboard. The questions, cadence, deliverables and capacity are defined as part of that arrangement.

name: Measurement strategy
lede: Agree what success means before asking your tools to report it.
intro: If every platform has its own version of success, it is difficult to know what marketing is contributing. I help your team define useful measures, map the evidence across systems and decide what needs to change to answer the important questions.
audience: Organisations with several marketing channels, a CRM or a longer sales process, and teams planning a website or reporting change.
signals: Enquiries are easy to count, but their quality and eventual outcomes are unclear.
Marketing and sales disagree about the meaning of a lead, customer or conversion.
You are planning a website or campaign and need a clear measurement brief before implementation.
deliverables: A decision and KPI framework
The management questions, success definitions and measures that deserve attention.
A map of the evidence
Which website, advertising, CRM or operational records can answer each question.
A measurement plan
Event and reporting requirements your team can use to brief implementation.
Attribution advice
A practical approach to known sources, CRM handovers, reporting periods and unknowns.
A prioritised roadmap
What to collect, repair, connect or investigate, with dependencies and ownership made clear.
value_heading: Connect the activity to the business question
value: This work helps you decide which measures to use, where better evidence is worth the effort and how marketing reporting should relate to real outcomes. It is particularly useful when a lead takes time to become a customer or when important steps happen outside the website.
process: Clarify the decisions
We work through your goals, existing reporting and the questions that currently cause uncertainty.
Map definitions and sources
I establish how important actions are recorded and where systems use different meanings or have gaps.
Agree the roadmap
You receive a practical framework and measurement brief, with implementation options and responsibilities.
boundary: Strategy defines the measurement approach. Tracking changes, dashboard development and integrations can follow as separate scoped work. Attribution will still have limits; unknown sources should remain visible rather than being assigned false precision.
proof_text: In a completed independent audit, I separated website activity, accepted enquiries, customer confirmation and payments. The recommendations identified which answers required operational records rather than additional GA4 events.
faqs: Do we need to replace our existing tools?
Not necessarily. The work starts with your decisions and current systems. A clearer definition or a better handover may be more useful than another platform.
Is this different from a GA4 audit?

An audit checks whether the current implementation is dependable. A measurement strategy defines what you should measure, where the evidence should come from and how it supports decisions. The scopes can be combined when useful.
Can you tell us exactly which channel caused every sale?
Not in every case. I help improve the available evidence and make the limits clear, including offline steps, returning visitors and unknown sources.
Can this start before a website rebuild?
Yes. A measurement brief can establish the required journeys, events and business definitions before your developer implements the new website.

name: Analytics support for agencies
lede: Add experienced measurement support while keeping a clear client relationship.
intro: When a client needs tracking, an audit or reporting expertise, you do not always need a permanent analytics hire. I work with agency teams on defined projects and ongoing support, from scoping the problem through to implementation, validation and explanation.
audience: Digital, creative, development and media agencies that need senior measurement support for their clients.
signals: Your developers can implement a brief, but need someone to define and validate the measurement.
A client has conflicting reports and needs a clear explanation before making a decision.
Your team needs additional analytics capacity across several projects without an undefined support commitment.
deliverables: Scoping and diagnosis
A practical assessment of the measurement problem and the work needed.
Technical collaboration
GA4/GTM configuration, developer briefs, selected journey testing and documented findings.
Client-ready explanation
Reports and recommendations your team can use in the client conversation.
A clear working arrangement
Agreement on scope, communication, client contact, deliverables and capacity before starting.
Continuity through documentation
A record of definitions, configuration, tests and dependencies for the next person working on the account.
value_heading: Specialist judgement your team can use
value: You work directly with me. I can contribute behind the scenes or alongside your team, depending on the arrangement. The aim is dependable measurement delivery and a clear handover, with your agency retaining the agreed commercial lead.
process: Brief the engagement
We establish the client problem, deliverables, working relationships and access.
Deliver within your workflow
I work with the relevant account, development and marketing people on the agreed scope.
Explain and hand over
Your team receives the evidence, implementation notes and a clear view of the next decisions.
boundary: White-label, joint delivery and ongoing capacity are options to agree, rather than assumptions. Availability, response expectations and additional work are confirmed for each arrangement.
proof_text: A recent agency assignment involved new practitioner-portal events, developer coordination, GTM configuration and staging checks in GA4. The work was documented at the point of validation, with the later production release left to the agency.
faqs: Can you work under our agency brand?
A behind-the-scenes or white-label arrangement can be agreed. We confirm how communication, attribution of work and client contact should operate before the engagement starts.
Can we bring you into a client meeting?
Yes, where it helps define the problem or explain the findings. We agree the role and communication approach with your team.
Do you provide one-off and ongoing support?
Both are possible. A project has a defined scope; ongoing work needs agreed capacity, priorities and deliverables.
Will you take over campaign management?
The core offer is measurement, analytics and reporting. Campaign delivery and wider agency responsibilities stay with the people you appoint.

name: Public sector & regulatory analytics
lede: Understand how your website supports the people who use it, with measures your team can explain.
intro: Website activity can help answer useful questions about information, journeys and service use. I help teams define those questions, improve the measurement and build reporting that makes its meaning and limitations clear.
audience: Digital, communications and reporting teams in public organisations and professional regulators, including work delivered through an agency partner.
signals: A board or leadership team needs website reporting with clear definitions and context.
A website or portal is changing and the useful journeys need to be measured consistently.
Reporting needs to explain service or information use without presenting clicks as wider public outcomes.
deliverables: A practical measurement brief
The website questions, audiences, journeys and success definitions in scope.
Tracking assurance or implementation
A review or configuration of selected events, with testing agreed around the website and its access controls.
Useful website reporting
A dashboard or reporting view with clear definitions, time coverage and interpretation.
Documentation and handover
Guidance your internal team or agency can use to maintain the agreed measurement.
Visible limitations
An explanation of what the website evidence can show and where other service or operational records are required.
value_heading: Useful evidence, with the context retained
value: The aim is reporting that supports a sensible discussion about website performance and service use. I bring relevant reporting experience for professional regulators and work directly with the people using the report or delivering the website. Access, handling of information and delivery requirements are agreed with your team.
process: Confirm the purpose and requirements
We identify the reporting audience, decisions, systems and any organisational requirements for the engagement.
Develop and review the evidence
I review the sources or implement the agreed measurement, working with your team or agency.
Document the result
You receive a clear explanation, relevant testing and handover material, with remaining dependencies recorded.
boundary: This is digital measurement and reporting support. Wider policy evaluation, causal programme-impact studies and formal privacy or security assurance require their own expertise and scope. The appropriate procurement route is confirmed by your organisation.
proof_text: I delivered a shared reporting dashboard for two professional regulators, with separate website views and a definitions page. Feedback on the draft informed the terminology and explanations, while differences in data coverage were made explicit.
faqs: Have you worked with regulatory organisations?

Yes. Relevant work includes website reporting for professional regulators and tracking delivery alongside an agency. Examples here are anonymised, and the scope of each is described without claiming a wider government endorsement.
Can you work through our existing agency?
Yes. I can contribute as a measurement specialist alongside an appointed development or digital agency, subject to the agreed delivery and procurement arrangements.
Will the report demonstrate the impact of a public programme?

Website evidence can show aspects of use and selected completed journeys. Wider impact may require service records, research or evaluation beyond website analytics. I help make that distinction clear.
Can you meet our information-handling requirements?
We review the relevant requirements, access and scope before agreeing the work. Any requirement needing another specialist or an approved supplier arrangement is identified during scoping.
